content_preview.summary: Angular's changelog dates 22.2.2 and 22.3.0-next.1 to October 8; the prerelease adds a @defer scrollMargin option and smart selection ranges for templates.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Angular project dated two releases October 8: version 22.2.2, a stable patch, and 22.3.0-next.1, a prerelease. According to the [Angular changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/main/CHANGELOG.md), 22.2.2 contains only fix and performance entries, while 22.3.0-next.1 carries the same entries plus two features, a `scrollMargin` option for `@defer` viewport triggers and smart selection ranges for templates in the language service. editor_notes.source_verification: Read from disk (gunzip) all three snapshots in sources/2026-10/angular-2222-ships-fixes-for-compiler-signal-forms-and-router-while-2230-next1-adds-a-scrollmargin-option-to-defer-viewport-options/. source-0.html.gz (CHANGELOG.md, 1,030,850 bytes, HTTP 200): the file begins with the 22.3.0-next.1 (2026-10-08) section and contains 22.2.2 (2026-10-08), 22.3.0-next.0 (2026-09-30) and 22.2.1 (2026-09-30) sections, so the rolling-file snapshot reflects the state at fetch time and contains the needed sections. I recounted: 22.2.2 has 18 'fix' rows and 1 'perf' row (compiler 6 fix; compiler-cli 1 fix + 1 perf; core 3; forms 4; language-service 1; router 3), matching the article's '18 fixes and one performance change'; 22.3.0-next.1 has 21 rows (the same set with a language-service fix reworded, plus 2 feat rows: core 'add `scrollMargin` to `@defer` viewport options' and language-service 'add smart selection ranges for templates'), matching '21 rows'. Every quoted entry title in the article matches the changelog text (HTML entities such as ' decode to the apostrophes used). Title claims: Compiler (6 fixes), Signal Forms ('use `Object.is` when comparing control bindings in signal forms' under forms) and Router (3 fixes) all appear among 22.2.2 fixes; the scrollMargin entry wording matches exactly and the changelog gives no default or rationale, as the article says. The language-service wording difference ('add strictUnclaimedEventNames to angularCompilerOptions schema' in 22.2.2 vs 'add missing options to angularCompilerOptions schema' in next.1) is correct. The router entry 'fall back when serializing protocol-relative URLs' appears in 22.2.1 (commit a6e6097b3d), 22.2.2 (576df28471) and 22.3.0-next.1 (a1bffc29dd) with different hashes and no explanation, as the article states. 22.3.0-next.0 (2026-09-30) entries quoted ('support increment/decrement operators in expressions', 'stop suppressing non-iterable values in `@for` expression') are present. source-1.html.gz (release v22.2.2 page, 200) and source-2.html.gz (release v22.3.0-next.1 page, 200) are real page bodies (about 4.5k chars of extracted text each, not just chrome): the next.1 page contains the scrollMargin and smart selection entries and a 'Pre-release' label; the 22.2.2 page contains the strictUnclaimedEventNames entry and a 'Latest' label. GitHub API check: v22.2.2 prerelease=false, published 2026-10-08T17:50:06Z; v22.3.0-next.1 prerelease=true, published 2026-10-08T18:07:15Z, matching the article. suspicious_patterns is null for all three sources; no instruction-like text found. Both domains (raw.githubusercontent.com, github.com) are already in config/source_allowlist.txt; no allowlist change needed.
